newsitem.title: INDIA: Khmer Rouge rebels selling arms to India rebels.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge rebels selling arms to India rebels.

text.p: Indian Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav said on Thursday that Cambodia's Khmer Rouge guerrillas were selling arms to separatist rebels operating in the remote northeast region of the country.

"Indian government came to know about the nexus between northeast rebels and Cambodian Khmer Rouge guerrillas following arrest of a few Indian rebels in the northeast," Yadav told reporters in Agartala, capital of Tripura state.
"Investigations revealed that Khmer Rouge guerrillas are selling arms to the northeast-based insurgent outfits," he said.
Yadav, who is on a visit to the northeastern states this week, did not elaborate.
Dozens of separatist groups in the northeast region are fighting for independent homelands.
India's northeastern region, comprising seven states with more than 200 ethnic groups and rich in minerals and timber, has been rocked by separatist violence for decades.

The hilly, heavily-forested northeast region is surrounded by Burma, Bangladesh, Bhutan and China, and linked to the rest of India by a 20-km (12-mile) wide corridor in the eastern state of West Bengal.
The government will take all measures to combat separatist violence in the northeast, Yadav said.
